bug_semantics: The advisory combines two x-proxy-path trust failures. In admin.ts, an attacker-controlled request header was inserted verbatim into served HTML, JavaScript, and CSS; because those header-dependent responses also lacked Vary and private/no-store cache controls, the reflection enabled direct or shared-cache-poisoning XSS on the admin origin. Separately, specialpages.ts passed a sanitizer that allowed leading slashes and then concatenated its result into a 302 Location. An x-proxy-path value of //evil.example therefore produced //evil.example/p/<encoded-pad>, which a browser follows as a protocol-relative cross-origin redirect.
flaw_origin: There are two independently introduced mechanisms. The admin reflection first appeared in human-authored commit 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d, not in the advisory's cited release-tip commit 63e9b2d4eb303cd341022591bdf9484584db36e3. The open-redirect mechanism first appeared when PR #7710 member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 changed a safe relative redirect into an absolute redirect prefixed by sanitizeProxyPath(req), whose then-current character filter preserved a leading //. That member was later represented on the main branch by squash commit 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29. The selected introducer is the smallest BIC for the advisory's AI-authored open-redirect component; the separate older admin-XSS origin is recorded for complete lifecycle attribution.
ai_marker: BIC commit object trailer: "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". The same object names author and committer John McLear <john@mclear.co.uk>; no inference from the later fix, PR body, branch name, or squash aggregate is needed.
evidence: Assigned first-party advisory GHSA-fjgc-3mj7-8rg8 / CVE-2026-55087 identifies affected ep_etherpad-lite >=2.1.0 through 3.0.0, first patched 3.1.0, the admin body substitutions in src/node/hooks/express/admin.ts, the legacy timeslider redirect in src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts, PRs #6399/#7710/#7784, and squash commits 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 and 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996: https://github.com/ether/etherpad/security/advisories/GHSA-fjgc-3mj7-8rg8

git log -L 77,82:src/node/hooks/express/admin.ts at fix parent b96e262782e1ed72999c42cb47fb9140e58fe544 and git log -S'req.header(PROXY_HEADER)' identify 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d as the first commit adding both raw replaceAll substitutions. Its direct parent is e6e1af58104b16a41fb500899e9a0bb50a7d1b85, whose admin handler used express.static/sendFile and contained neither x-proxy-path reading nor response-body substitution. git show confirms 63e9b2d4eb303cd341022591bdf9484584db36e3 touched APIHandler.ts, Settings.ts, tsort.js, and pnpm-lock.yaml, not admin.ts.
git tag --contains 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d starts at 2.1.0/v2.1.0 and includes every affected release through 3.0.0, matching the admin-XSS boundary.

The first-party PR #7710 commit list and local commit objects decompose mainline squash 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 to member f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 for the vulnerable redirect: https://github.com/ether/etherpad/pull/7710/commits. git log -L 404,415:src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts at f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 shows that exact member replacing return res.redirect(302, `../${encodeURIComponent(req.params.pad)}`) with const proxyPath = sanitizeProxyPath(req) followed by return res.redirect(302, `${proxyPath}/p/${encodeURIComponent(req.params.pad)}`).

Direct parent-tree comparison f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2^ = c5a54cfd7b528186aca33aea971b7099ca468790 proves the header-derived Location construction absent: the parent used only the fixed relative ../<encoded-pad> target. At that parent, src/node/hooks/express/specialpages.ts:25-27 defined sanitizeProxyPath as raw.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\-_\/\.]/g, ''), which preserved //; f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 was the first commit to feed that output into Location.

git cat-file commit f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 records parent c5a54cfd7b528186aca33aea971b7099ca468790, author/committer John McLear, and the exact Claude Opus 4.7 Co-Authored-By trailer. This is the only evidence used for AI attribution.

git show of mainline squash 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 contains the same final header-derived redirect, and git tag --contains 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 starts at 3.0.0/v3.0.0, so the decomposed BIC's patch first shipped in 3.0.0 as the advisory states.

PR head 29fd3b3638f60342da34bcf4a3bd2c8c269e7e1b has a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 as its parent; GitHub landed the PR as squash 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996: https://github.com/ether/etherpad/pull/7784 and https://github.com/ether/etherpad/commit/8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing separates the GHSA's two causal paths rather than treating its cited commits as authoritative BICs. For admin XSS, history follows the vulnerable replaceAll lines to 3e9c90e994d4af71ac8f49668f48caf61ef1b55d and directly verifies their absence in e6e1af58104b16a41fb500899e9a0bb50a7d1b85; that origin is human and predates v2.1.0. For the open redirect, the mainline 451bd9c3ebb0dded99dd0ff21811ee00e0940c29 object is a squash aggregate, so it is not accepted as the BIC. PR-member lineage shows that earlier members created a relative redirect, while f784c8c47c16e184b3ef3bdbf84485d4e5c42eb2 alone changed it to the header-prefixed absolute Location. Its immediate parent retained the relative form, making parent absence direct and unambiguous. The corresponding squash first appears in v3.0.0. The direct security member a6de73c8f90a75289de35f7585165a361ba54f28 removes both mechanisms, and landed as 8c6104c5d5daf41f0d454acc04d42dffa0e0d996 in v3.1.0. Finally, the smallest selected BIC's own commit object explicitly co-attributes Claude Opus 4.7. Because that AI-coauthored BIC first wrote the flawed header-to-Location data flow, the open-redirect component meets AI_ROOT_CAUSE. The verdict does not attribute the independently human-origin admin-XSS component to AI and does not rely on the AI-assisted fix.
